## Keyboard Clicker 2.0.0

This is the first release of the new Rust desktop application. The original Python application remains in the repository.

### Highlights

- Build ordered automation sequences from mouse clicks, key presses, text entry, and timed waits.
- Reorder and enable/disable steps; set a finite repeat count or run continuously until stopped.
- Configure global start/stop hotkeys, including modifier combinations; F6/F7 are the defaults.
- Use dark/light appearance, a custom accent color, and English, German, or Russian UI text. Additional JSON translations are supported.
- Store settings per user, without administrator privileges.
- Run on 64-bit Windows 10/11 and x86_64 Linux.

### Downloads

- **Windows x64:** download `keyboard-clicker-windows-x86_64.zip`, extract it, and run `keyboard-clicker.exe`.
- **Linux x86_64:** download and extract `keyboard-clicker-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.

Each archive has an adjacent `.sha256` file. Verify the checksum before launching a downloaded build.

The Windows executable is unsigned. Linux input automation currently relies on X11; native Wayland input support varies by compositor. See the README for platform notes, prerequisites, and build instructions.

### Verification

The release workflow runs the test suite on Windows and Linux before packaging platform builds. Each platform archive is attached by the release workflow.
